title: Sell Mineral Rights in Benwood, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Benwood, WV | Marshall County
metaDescription: Benwood, WV sits in Marshall County, one of the heaviest-producing Marcellus counties. We buy mineral rights and royalty interests here directly.
heroLead: Benwood is a small river town in Marshall County, and Marshall County is not a marginal player in this play, it's one of the highest-volume Marcellus and Utica producing counties in the country.
intro: That volume matters for mineral owners. Marshall County has seen dense horizontal well pad development, large pooled units, and heavy processing infrastructure sited nearby, which means a Benwood-area mineral interest is more likely than most to be actively producing rather than sitting idle under an old, unused lease.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Benwood directly, and because this county has so much active production, we put real weight on checking your unit's actual well status and payment history before we price your interest.

sections.heading: A heavily developed county changes the math
paragraphs: In a county with this much lateral drilling and pooling, a mineral tract can be swept into a unit with multiple producing wells, which changes the value calculation substantially compared to an interest sitting under a single legacy well. We check how many wells are actually completed in your unit and where they stand in their production curve before naming a figure.

sections.heading: Industrial river town, fractionalized ownership
paragraphs: Benwood's history as a steel and manufacturing town means a lot of mineral ownership here traces back to family farms that predate the industry, later split among heirs who scattered as the mills changed hands. It's common to find eight or more co-owners on a single small tract.

sections.heading: Checking royalty statement mechanics
paragraphs: If you're already receiving royalty checks on a Benwood-area interest, the check stub itself tells us a lot: decimal interest, unit designation, and deduction language. We read those details before making an offer so the number reflects what the well is actually producing, not a rough county-wide estimate.

faqs.question: Marshall County has a lot of drilling. Does that mean my interest is worth more automatically?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Value depends on how many producing wells sit in your specific unit, your decimal interest, and where those wells are in their decline curve.

faqs.question: I get royalty checks but don't understand the deductions on them.
faqs.answer: Post-production cost deductions vary by lease. We review your check stub and the underlying lease language as part of evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: Can you buy just my share if there are several co-owners?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly purchase individual undivided fractional interests without requiring co-owners to sell together.
